text:
maria: Heads up — since ~13:12 UTC we're seeing apiserver connection drops in us-west1. Kubelet reconnect loops and controller-manager lease renewals are spiking.
kevin: I see increased apiserver 502 and client-side dial timeouts in the logs. Any recent infra changes?
maria: No deploys around that time. We had a burst of GPU node scale-ups in the region (dedicated pools) which correlated with the first errors.
anika: can you paste the apiserver logs snippet?
maria: sure, here's the tail from one apiserver pod: ```
E0318 13:12:34.123456       1 round_trippers.go:520] canceling request due to error: net/http: TLS handshake timeout
W0318 13:12:35.654321       1 controller_manager.go:275] Failed to renew lease: context deadline exceeded
E0318 13:12:36.000001       1 trace.go:116] Trace[12345]: "Get /api/v1/namespaces/default/pods" (started: 2026-03-18 13:12:34.123) (total time: 2.500s)
```
leo: that TLS handshake timeout with multiple kubelets smells like control-plane network churn (ENI detach/reattach/route propagation) during node scale operations.
jasper: also saw etcd leader election jitter around the same time: leader changes ~4x in 5m. Might amplify load on apiserver.
srebot: incident created: INC-2026-0318-01 (apiserver partial degradation — us-west1) :rotating_light:
maria: confirmed. Controller-manager CPU also spiked as it retried. We're getting a feedback loop: apiserver slow -> controllers retry -> more apiserver load.
kevin: action items: 1) short-term: add client-side keepalive and bump apiserver QPS/burst for controllers, 2) stabilize etcd leader by increasing election timeout slightly, 3) reduce scale-up burst for GPU pools.
anika: agree. For (1) we can patch controller-manager args: --kube-api-qps=100 --kube-api-burst=200 and enable keepalives in the kubeclient where possible.
leo: for (2) we should avoid changing etcd timeouts too often; maybe use a small increase: --etcd-election-timeout from 2500ms to 4000ms and observe. That reduces leader churn during transient network noise.
jasper: I'll throttle autoscaler: change GPU pool max-surge from 50 to 8 for the next hour and enable a 30s batching window so we don't create many ENIs at once.
maria: deploying throttle now. Also spinning a canary of apiserver with more aggressive acceptor backlog and keepalive settings to test.
kevin: db/ops note: check control-plane host-level NIC metrics and cloud API errors (attach/detach rate-limits) — if cloud is rate-limiting ENI ops that's the root cause.
anika: logging note: we should also add a short-lived sampler to capture full request traces for the next 30m so we can see which controllers caused the retry storm.
leo: temporary mitigation: enable automatic fallback routing for read-only requests to a read-replica LB endpoint to reduce pressure on default apiservers.
jasper: rolling restart of controller-manager planned at +15m after throttle.
maria: update: throttle applied, apiserver error rates down a bit. etcd leader stable for 2 min. continuing monitoring.
srebot: update INC-2026-0318-01: mitigations applied — autoscaler throttle, controller-manager patch queued, apiserver canary deployed.
deploy-bot: canary apiserver patched and rolled to 1 pod in us-west1-canary. Link: https://console.internal/redeploy/1979812345
kevin: follow-ups: 1) longer-term: add ENI attach/detach smoothing to autoscaler, 2) test raising etcd electionTimeout under small network blips, 3) refine controller QPS defaults in docs.
anika: I'll write a short postmortem template with timeline and signal graphs. Assigning action owners in the doc.
maria: thanks all. keeping channel open until full recovery. :thumbsup:
